LESSON: REPRODUCTION IN PLANTS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Living things and their Environment
Topic 2.3: Reproduction in plants

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reproduction in plants. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How does reproduction in plants occur?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain fertilisation and fruit formation in flowering plants
2. recognise the role of flowers in nature

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: REPRODUCTION IN PLANTS
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reproduction in plants helps you succeed in INTEGRATED SCIENCE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS ABOUT PLANTS
Roots hold the plant and take in water. Leaves help the plant make food using sunlight.
Kenyan examples: maize, beans, sukuma wiki, bananas, mango trees.
Without water and light, most seedlings wilt.

PART 1: Explain fertilisation and fruit formation in flowering plants

What this means
In this part you learn to explain fertilisation and fruit formation in flowering plants. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain fertilisation and fruit formation in flowering plants.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Reproduction in plants” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain fertilisation and fruit formation in flowering plants. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Recognise the role of flowers in nature

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise the role of flowers in nature. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise the role of flowers in nature.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Reproduction in plants matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise the role of flowers in nature. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reproduction in plants is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Roots hold the plant and take in water. Leaves help the plant make food using sunlight.

Kenyan examples: maize, beans, sukuma wiki, bananas, mango trees.

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Reproduction in plants” around your school. (skill: explain fertilisation and fruit formation in flowering plants)

Example 2: Say why Reproduction in plants matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: recognise the role of flowers in nature)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reproduction in plants to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain fertilisation and fruit formation in flowering plants.
3. Practise this skill: recognise the role of flowers in nature.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reproduction in plants from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reproduction in plants: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Reproduction in plants?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How does reproduction in plants occur?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reproduction in plants means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain fertilisation and fruit formation in flowering plants.
5. Be able to: recognise the role of flowers in nature.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
